note: The Brooklyn Bridge and DUMBO: four hero kits (runs/brooklyn-bridge, built through the Message Batches API): the Brooklyn Bridge (tower, deck section, main-span and side-span cables with their stays, anchorage, approach section) laid straight along z at x 723..740; the Manhattan Bridge (tower, deck section, cables, anchorage with the Archway) laid straight and turned 20.6 degrees as one group onto its line; the Clock Tower Building and Empire Stores with Jane's Carousel, each built square on DUMBO's grid and turned 46.1 degrees back onto its footprint; batched Haiku fill (bin/fill.mjs --batch) on DUMBO, Fulton Ferry and the Manhattan blocks by the bridge, the DUMBO ones turned the same way; the Lower Manhattan skyline stays lidar massing.
common: Scale: 0.7 blocks per metre (a storey is about 2.5 blocks). For a public catalog for a Minecraft 1.21.1 server: only blocks that exist in 1.21.1 (no pale oak, no "iron_chain" (it is "chain" in 1.21.1), nothing 1.21.4+). These are real structures of the Brooklyn waterfront in New York for a hero AERIAL render at golden hour: the camera looks from high over the East River and Brooklyn Bridge Park toward the Brooklyn Bridge with the Lower Manhattan skyline behind, so silhouettes, tops and the faces toward the river matter most. Placement code sets each module exactly where the real one stands, so every dimension and coordinate below is exact; keep to them. Exterior only: no interiors beyond what shows through glass. No villagers. Nothing may leave its plot or exceed its stated height. Light it for dusk (lamps on the bridge decks and promenade, warm windows in some lofts, floodlit stone) so no mob spawns on a walkable surface.
closing: Use the photograph only as inspiration for character and colour; the dimensions above are exact.

kits.intro: The Brooklyn Bridge (1883, John A. and Washington Roebling), New York: the great suspension bridge over the East River from Manhattan to Brooklyn. It must read, at a glance, as THIS bridge: two massive grey-buff granite and limestone towers, each pierced by TWIN POINTED GOTHIC ARCHES; four pale main cables sweeping between them; and the famous web of cables: the vertical suspenders crossed by the DIAGONAL STAYS that fan out from each tower top; the elevated wooden promenade running down the middle above the two roadways. These are kit modules: placement code drops each one onto the real bridge line and repeats the deck section and the approach section along it.
kits.frame:
THE KIT'S FRAME (all six plots): the bridge runs along z (Manhattan is low z, Brooklyn high z; east is high x). VERTICAL DATUM: y 0 is the river's surface; placement drops the y 0 layer (the river stays there), so build NOTHING that matters at y 0, and lay no ground course: every cell not part of the bridge stays air.
SHARED DECK CROSS-SECTION (18 wide, in the deck's own x 0..17; plot 0 and plot 4 hold it at their local x 8..25): the two OUTER cable lines are x 0 and x 17, the two INNER cable lines x 6 and x 11. Two roadways x 1..5 and x 12..16, road surface at y 27 (dark grey: gray concrete / polished blackstone, faint white lane marks), cars at y 28. The PROMENADE: a raised boardwalk of warm wood planks (spruce or oak) at y 30, x 7..10, between the inner cable lines, with dark iron railings (fences or iron bars) at y 31 on x 7 and x 10, and the classic Victorian lamp posts (dark iron posts with a lantern) on its edges. The stiffening trusses: a lattice truss along each cable line from y 22 to y 29 (pale tan-grey steel: smooth sandstone / birch planks / mushroom stem or similar warm pale tones), floor beams and bracing under the roadways at y 22..26. Cable and stay colour everywhere: pale grey-white (white concrete, smooth quartz, light grey) so the web reads against the sky; thin members as iron bars, chains (vertical only), walls or panes as you judge best, always 8-connected (no gaps on a diagonal).

plots.label: THE TOWER (used for both towers)
plots.text: the masonry tower standing in the river on its caisson. The deck passes through it along z at local x 8..25 (deck x 0..17). Tower body x 2..31 (30 wide), z 3..16 (14 deep) at the water, stepping in gently with height so its top stage (above y 48) is z 5..14; granite and limestone in grey-buff and warm grey (stone bricks, tuff bricks, polished andesite, smooth sandstone or similar), coursed and rusticated, with string courses and a heavy projecting cornice at y 55..57; flat top at y 58 with a low parapet. THE TWIN POINTED ARCHES: two tall Gothic pointed-arch openings through the full depth of the tower, x 8..14 and x 19..25 (7 wide each), from the road level (y 27) up to their pointed crowns at y 48, with deep moulded arch rings (recessed orders) and a pointed hood over each; the central pier x 15..18 between them, the outer piers x 2..7 and x 26..31; each face of the piers has tall slender recessed Gothic panels above the arches. The roadways run through the arches at y 27; the promenade boardwalk (y 30) splits to pass the central pier on both sides (x 14 and x 19) and widens into small overlooks against the pier. Below the deck the tower is solid down to the caisson. THE CAISSON: a rough granite base x 0..33, z 0..19 from y 1 to y 3. THE CABLES OVER THE TOP: the four main cables pass over the tower top in saddles at y 57 on x 8, 14, 19 and 25; on both faces they emerge from the masonry just below the cornice and run out to the plot's ends, sloping down to y 54 at z 0 and at z 19 (one block thick, pale, 8-connected). Leave every other cell of z 0..2 and z 17..19 above y 3 empty (the deck sections and the cable modules join there).

plots.label: THE DECK SECTION (repeated end to end along z)
plots.text: exactly the shared cross-section, x 0..17, along all of z 0..15; its two ends (z 0 and z 15) must join seamlessly with copies of itself. Roadways at y 27, promenade boards at y 30 with railings at y 31, trusses y 22..29 on x 0, 6, 11, 17, floor beams beneath. One pair of promenade lamp posts at z 8 (on x 7 and x 10, lantern about y 34). Suspender anchor points on the truss tops at z 0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15 on the four cable lines (y 29). Nothing below y 22, nothing above y 36.

plots.label: THE MAIN-SPAN CABLES (one half of the main span; placed twice)
plots.text: ONLY the cables, suspenders and stays, nothing else (this module is laid over the repeated deck). Local z 0 is mid-span; local z 159 is right next to the tower's face (the tower's centre is at z 169.5). With u = z + 0.5, each of the four main cables, on x 0, 6, 11 and 17, runs at height y(u) = 33 + 24 * (u / 170)^2: z 0: 33.0, 40: 34.4, 80: 38.4, 120: 45.2, 140: 49.3, 159: 54.0. Draw each as one continuous, smooth line of pale blocks softened with slabs and stairs, filled vertically where steep so it stays 8-connected, with cable bands every 6. SUSPENDERS: thin vertical pale lines every 3 blocks (z = 0, 3, 6, ...) on all four cable lines, from just under the cable down to y 29. THE DIAGONAL STAYS (the bridge's signature): in each of the four cable planes, 16 straight stays fan out from the tower face: each starts at z 159 between y 50 and y 55 (spread evenly up the tower face) and runs straight down to land on the deck at y 29 at z 153, 147, 141, ... 63 (every 6 blocks); 1 block thick, pale, 8-connected (a line in the y-z plane: a staircase of blocks or slabs), crossing the suspenders and each other to form the web.

plots.label: THE SIDE-SPAN CABLES (tower to anchorage; placed twice)
plots.text: ONLY the cables, suspenders and stays. Local z 0 is right next to the tower's face (the tower's centre is at z -10.5); local z 175 is at the anchorage's face, where the cables enter it. With t = (z + 11) / 186.5, each main cable on x 0, 6, 11 and 17 runs at y(t) = 57 - 33 t - 16 t (1 - t): z 0: 54.2, 22: 49.2, 44: 43.9, 66: 39.4, 88: 35.5, 110: 32.0, 132: 28.8, 154: 26.2, 175: 24.0; same look as the main span. SUSPENDERS every 3 blocks on all four lines from just under the cable down to the deck's truss top, which steps down every 16: z 0..15: y 29; 16..31: 28; 32..63: 27; 64..79: 26; 80..111: 25; 112..143: 24; 144..159: 23; 160..175: 22. DIAGONAL STAYS: in each cable plane, 12 straight stays from the tower face (z 0, between y 50 and 55, spread) down to the deck truss top at z 6, 12, 18, ... 72. Keep every member above the deck's railings.

plots.label: THE ANCHORAGE (used at both ends)
plots.text: the massive granite anchorage where the four cables are anchored, its road on top. Local z 0 faces the bridge (the side-span cables arrive there). A great block of grey-buff granite x 2..31, z 2..29, from y 0 up to the road at y 20 (the street around it is at about y 4..7; build it solid down to y 0, the part below the street is buried), battered walls, rusticated quoins, a strong cornice under the parapets, and on each long side (x 2 and x 31) three tall round-arched recessed vaults reaching from y 4 to about y 15. ON TOP: the deck cross-section continues along z 0..29 at local x 8..25 at road level y 20 (roadways at y 20, promenade boards at y 23 with railings), between solid granite parapets 2 high on x 2..7 and x 26..31. THE CABLE ENTRIES: on the bridge-facing end the four cables (local x 8, 14, 19, 25) arrive at y 24 at z 0 and enter low granite cable housings (3 wide, 4 deep, up to y 25) that stand on the parapet line and beside the promenade at z 0..3, so the roadways stay clear.

plots.label: THE APPROACH SECTION (repeated end to end along z, stepping down to the street)
plots.text: the masonry approach viaduct carrying the deck from the anchorage down to the street; its two ends (z 0 and z 15) join seamlessly with copies of itself. Road level y 20 across x 0..17: the deck cross-section on stone (roadways x 1..5 and x 12..16 at y 20, the promenade boards x 7..10 at y 23 with railings and a lamp pair at z 8), granite parapets 2 high on x 0 and x 17; beneath it solid granite masonry from y 0 to y 19, with one big round-arched vault through it along x (open from x 0 to x 17) spanning z 3..12 up to y 12, as the real approach's arches over the streets. Placement lowers it into the ground as the road descends, so the lower part may be buried: build it solid, coursed, with a cornice under the parapets.

kits.intro: The Manhattan Bridge (1909, Leon Moisseiff, with Carrère and Hastings), New York: the steel suspension bridge just upriver of the Brooklyn Bridge, the one framed at the end of Washington Street in DUMBO. It must read, at a glance, as THIS bridge: two tall STEEL TOWERS painted pale blue-grey, each a pair of riveted legs with lattice X-bracing between them and an ornamental Beaux-Arts crown of arched cross-girders with ball-topped finials; four cables; a deep double-deck truss (roadways on top, subway tracks below); and the massive granite anchorages, the Brooklyn one pierced by the tall vaulted ARCHWAY over a cobbled plaza. These are kit modules: placement lays them out along the bridge line and turns them onto it.
kits.frame:
THE KIT'S FRAME (all five plots): the bridge runs along z (Manhattan is low z). VERTICAL DATUM: y 0 is the river's surface; placement drops the y 0 layer, so build nothing that matters at y 0 and lay no ground course; every cell not part of the bridge stays air.
SHARED DECK CROSS-SECTION (24 wide, the deck's own x 0..23; plot 0 holds it at local x 2..25, plot 4 at local x 5..28): four cable lines and four deep trusses at x 1, 8, 15 and 22. UPPER LEVEL: two roadways x 2..7 and x 16..21, road surface at y 29 (dark grey with lane marks), outer walkway / bike path strips at x 0 and x 23 with railings at y 30. LOWER LEVEL: subway tracks under the upper roadways (rails on gravel at y 23, x 2..7 and x 16..21) and the lower roadway x 9..14 at y 23. The four trusses: riveted Warren trusses (diagonals) from y 22 to y 31 on x 1, 8, 15, 22, top chords at y 31. Steel colour everywhere: pale blue-grey (light blue terracotta, light gray concrete, with darker cyan terracotta or gray for shadowed members); cables pale grey; thin members as iron bars, walls or panes, 8-connected.

plots.label: THE STEEL TOWER (used for both towers)
plots.text: the tower on its granite pier in the river; the deck passes through it along z at local x 2..25 (deck x 0..23). THE PIER: granite x 0..27, z 0..11 from y 1 to y 8 with a rounded cutwater at each z end. THE LEGS: two riveted steel legs rising from the pier, x 1..6 and x 21..26, each a box of four latticed columns, z 3..8 at the bottom narrowing to z 4..7 at the top, up to y 66. Between the legs above the deck: lattice X-bracing (diagonal members in the x-y plane on z 5..6) in three panels between y 34 and y 58, with horizontal struts at y 33, 46 and 58. THE CROWN (y 58..71): a Beaux-Arts top: a deep arched cross-girder joining the leg tops (its underside an arch from x 7 to x 20 rising to y 62), the leg tops capped with stepped cornices and tall ball-topped finials to y 71 on each leg. THE CABLES: four saddles on the crown at y 63 on local x 3, 10, 17 and 24; the cables leave both faces (z 0 and z 11) at y 62 and the cable modules continue them. The deck (the shared cross-section, roadways y 29, lower level y 23) runs straight through between the legs along all of z 0..11.

plots.label: THE DECK SECTION (repeated end to end along z)
plots.text: exactly the shared cross-section, x 0..23, along all of z 0..11, both ends joining seamlessly with copies of itself: upper roadways at y 29, lower level at y 23, the four Warren trusses y 22..31 (one diagonal panel every 6 blocks, verticals at z 0 and z 6), floor beams under each level, railings, and one pair of lamp posts at z 6 on the outer walkways. Suspender anchor points on the truss top chords (y 31) at z 0, 3, 6, 9 on the four cable lines. Nothing below y 22, nothing above y 34.

plots.label: THE MAIN-SPAN CABLES (one half of the main span; placed twice)
plots.text: ONLY the four cables and their suspenders (no stays: this bridge has none), laid over the repeated deck. Local z 0 is mid-span; local z 149 is next to the tower's face (the tower's centre at z 155.5). With u = z + 0.5, each cable on x 1, 8, 15 and 22 runs at y(u) = 37 + 26 (u / 156)^2: z 0: 37.0, 40: 38.7, 80: 43.8, 120: 52.4, 149: 60.9; one continuous smooth pale line each, softened with slabs and stairs, 8-connected, cable bands every 6. SUSPENDERS: thin vertical pale lines every 3 blocks on all four cable lines from just under the cable down to y 32 (the truss tops).

plots.label: THE SIDE-SPAN CABLES (tower to anchorage; placed twice)
plots.text: ONLY the four cables and their suspenders. Local z 0 is next to the tower's face (the tower's centre at z -6.5); local z 143 is at the anchorage's face. With t = (z + 6.5) / 150.5, each cable on x 1, 8, 15 and 22 runs at y(t) = 63 - 32 t - 12 t (1 - t): z 0: 61.1, 36: 52.4, 72: 43.4, 108: 36.5, 143: 31.2. SUSPENDERS every 3 blocks from under the cable down to the truss tops: z 0..35: y 32; 36..107: y 31; 108..143: y 30.

plots.label: THE ANCHORAGE WITH THE ARCHWAY (used at both ends)
plots.text: the massive granite anchorage; local z 0 faces the bridge (the side-span cables arrive there at y 31 on local x 6, 13, 20, 27 and enter the masonry). A great block of buff-grey granite x 0..33, z 0..39 from y 0 up to the deck at y 27 (the street around it is at about y 4..7; build it solid down to y 0), with rusticated walls, pilasters and a deep cornice at y 24..26, and parapets up to y 29. THE ARCHWAY: a tall barrel-vaulted passage straight through the anchorage across the bridge's axis (along x, open from x 0 to x 33) spanning z 14..25, its round arch rising from y 5 to its crown at y 19, the vault coffered, with a cobblestone plaza floor at y 5 (cobblestone, mossy cobblestone, stone bricks) and lamps inside; rusticated voussoirs and a keystone on both arch faces. ON TOP: the deck's upper level continues at local x 5..28 at y 27 (roadways and walkways, railings), the cables' anchor housings at z 0..4.

kits.intro: The Clock Tower Building, 1 Main Street, DUMBO, Brooklyn (1915, built for Robert Gair's carton company; condominiums since 2000): a white reinforced-concrete loft building on the waterfront crowned by a slim four-faced CLOCK TOWER. It must read, at a glance, as THIS building: a big, plain, pale-cream concrete block of about 15 storeys, its facades a regular grid of large industrial windows between flat concrete piers and spandrels; on top, the square tower with a huge round clock face on each side (white dial, black hands and numerals, glowing at dusk) under a small cornice and pyramidal cap.
kits.frame: THE PLOT'S FRAME: DUMBO's own street grid: north (low z) is true north, toward the East River and Water Street; Main Street runs along the west edge (low x), Plymouth Street along the south (high z) and Washington Street to the east (high x). Placement turns the module 46.1 degrees back onto the real footprint, so build it square in this frame.

plots.label: THE CLOCK TOWER BUILDING
plots.text: follow the ROOF HEIGHT map for the massing: the main block and any lower wings, and the clock tower where the lidar rises highest (its top about 58 blocks over the ground): the tower about 9 x 9 rising above the main roof with a clock face about 7 across, centred, on each of its four sides; the main facades: pale cream / off-white concrete (white concrete, smooth quartz, calcite, bone block, or similar), a regular grid of big multi-pane factory windows (glass panes with thin dark frames), the piers and spandrels flat and slightly proud, a simple cornice band at the roofline, a slightly richer ground floor with entrances on Main and Washington Streets. Warm light in some windows; light the clock faces from behind.

kits.intro: Empire Stores and Jane's Carousel, DUMBO, Brooklyn: the waterfront heart of Brooklyn Bridge Park between the two bridges. EMPIRE STORES (1869-1885): a long row of seven joined brick coffee and sugar warehouses, five storeys, on Water Street facing the river: deep red-brown brick walls, rows of round-arched and segmental-arched window openings with heavy iron shutters (dark green / black) pinned open, granite sills and lintels, stone quoins, a stepped and corbelled roofline over each warehouse bay, and since 2017 a cut through its middle to a green roof garden. JANE'S CAROUSEL (1922 Philadelphia Toboggan carousel; pavilion by Jean Nouvel, 2011): a vintage painted carousel in a clear GLASS BOX pavilion on the riverside lawn, a flat black-edged roof over a tall transparent cube, the carousel's lights glowing inside at dusk. They must read, at a glance, as THESE: the long red-brick arcade of shuttered openings beside the river, and the glowing glass box.
kits.frame: THE PLOTS' FRAME: DUMBO's own street grid: north (low z) is true north, toward the East River; Water Street runs along x on the south side of Empire Stores. Placement turns each module 46.1 degrees back onto its real footprint, so build them square in this frame.

plots.label: EMPIRE STORES
plots.text: five storeys of brick warehouse over the whole footprint (follow the ROOF HEIGHT map), divided along x into seven warehouse bays each with its own stepped, corbelled gable-parapet top; the north (river) and south (Water Street) facades: rows of tall arched openings, one bay of openings every 3 blocks, with iron shutters (dark spruce or dark oak trapdoors set open beside each window, or dark green / black blocks), glass behind; granite string courses; the ground floor with big arched loading doors, now shopfronts, warm-lit; the roof: a green roof garden with planters, lawn and a few small trees over the middle bays, reached by an open cut through the building in the middle of its length.

plots.label: JANE'S CAROUSEL
plots.text: the clear glass pavilion over the whole footprint: a square box of glass (glass blocks or white-framed glass panes), about 7 blocks high, a thin flat roof with a black edge, a low concrete plinth; inside, centred, the round carousel about 13 across: a ring floor, a central drum with mirrors and painted panels (colourful: red, gold, white, cream), a conical striped canopy roof, carved horses (use colourful blocks, banners or armour-stand-free shapes) around the platform, and a ring of warm lights (lanterns, glowstone, shroomlights) under the canopy so the whole box glows.
